title: tracing-roadshow-handoff-brief-2028-12-05
content:
Context:
This doc captures notes from the small-format 'tracing roadshow' we ran with Console, SRE, and Platform last week. Goal: reduce span cardinality and trace storage cost while keeping SLO signal fidelity for latency regressions. This is a working handoff for the next two-week sprint (oncall rotations + dashboard refresh).

Attendees:
- Aisha Kumar (OBS, owner)
- Benji Park (SRE)
- Marta Alvarez (Console)
- Ravi Shen (Serving runtime)
- Jen Cho (Platform eng)
- Guests: Priya (Dedicated), Lou (Evaluate)

TL;DR summary:
- Agreed on a two-pronged approach: tighten sampling on high-cardinality spans + introduce derived metrics in dashboards to preserve alert sensitivity.
- Experiment alpha (trace-sample-heatmap) reduced stored traces by ~43% in staging without losing 95th pct latency signal.
- Action items allocated; owners and Linear tickets listed below.

What we tested / findings:
1) Heatmap-guided sampling (Ravi/B. Park)
- Config: dynamic sample rate per span family based on 7-day frequency histogram; floor 0.5% and ceil 100%.
- Staging run: 2028-11-28 -> 2028-12-03.
- Result: stored spans down 43%, raw traces down 37%. 95th/99th p90 latency alerts still triggered on identical incidents in synthetic replay.
- Notes: some early user-debug traces missing for a low-volume Kafka fanout path. We need a short retention override for user-initiated trace ids.

2) Derived error-rate counters inside ingestion (Marta)
- Instead of relying on full traces to compute error-rate by route, we created per-request derived counters at ingestion.
- Dashboard panels switched to use counters for alerting; traces still used for RCA.
- Benefit: alerting stable across sampling changes; cost for counters is negligible.

3) Dashboard refresh and panel rationalization (Jen)
- Consolidated three per-model dashboards into one model-perf grid; reduced panel duplication.
- New panels: "Sampled traces per minute", "Derived errors by route", "Trace storage delta (24h)".
- Removed: high-cardinality tag breakdowns that were rarely used.

Open questions / risks:
- User debugability: if we drop traces too aggressively, support engineers lose the ability to reproduce rare client issues. Proposal: implement a 72h trace-retention override API that can be triggered from Console (Marta). Ticket: INF-4489.
- Long tail costs from async workers: several low-volume async paths still emit large span trees. Need a quick audit to identify top 10 offending spans. (Action: Ravi to run span-topology audit: INF-4511)
- Instrumentation debt: some libs still set span attributes with high-cardinality user IDs. We should add linting in the repo to catch new attributes and surface them to authors during code review. (Action: Benji)

Decisions taken:
- Adopt heatmap-guided sampling as default in staging and a canary rollout to prod for 25% of traffic on Mon 2028-12-11.
- Switch primary latency alert to be based on derived metrics and maintain a secondary trace-based verification alert.
- Implement short-term Console button to "archive traces for 72h" for a trace id; explore RBAC gating for this feature.

Action items (owner -> ticket -> ETA):
- Ravi Shen -> INF-4511 -> 2028-12-08: run span-topology audit, produce top 10 high-cardinality span families and suggested attribute reductions.
- Benji Park -> INF-4478 -> 2028-12-10: add instrumentation-linter rule and a pre-commit hook prototype; roll out to two repos.
- Marta Alvarez -> INF-4489 -> 2028-12-15: Console "archive traces" MVP spec + design for RBAC.
- Jen Cho -> INF-4528 -> 2028-12-12: migrate three dashboards to the new model-perf grid and retire deprecated panels.
- Aisha Kumar -> INF-4530 -> 2028-12-09: prepare roll-out plan for canary sampling (25% prod traffic) and runbook for oncall.
- Oncall (rotation): week of 2028-12-11 -> Benji / Aisha primary, Ravi backup.

Runbook excerpts (to copy into oncall handbook):
- If alert fires and traces absent: check "Derived errors by route" panel. If derived metric also spikes, treat as true positive and follow RCA play.
- If alert fires and derived metric is flat: increase sampling for the route (Console action) by 5x for 30 minutes; notify OBS channel and capture debug traces.
- If missing user-repro trace requested by Support: enable "archive traces for 72h" and ask Support to reproduce.

Short notes on cost telemetry implications:
- Current storage bill baseline (Nov average): $18.6k/month. Projection with heatmap sampling at scale: $10.5k/month (best estimate).
- Impact on compute (ingestion counters): +2% CPU across ingestion cluster; negligible compared to storage savings.
- Next invoice cycle we should tag traces with sampling-policy metadata to attribute cost to product teams (Jen ticket INF-4555).

Follow-ups for next meeting (2028-12-12):
- Ravi to present audit results and proposed attribute removals.
- Marta to demo Console archive button prototype.
- Benji to show linter PR and initial false-positive analysis.
- Jen to provide dashboard migration checklist and rollback steps.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep the staging run for an extra 48h if holiday traffic looks different; initial synthetic tests looked promising but we still need 1 full real-prod weekday.
- Remember to ping legal about potential PII in archived traces (privacy check).

References and links:
- Linear board: INF-4182 (tracing cost program), INF-4511, INF-4489
- GitHub: /telemetry PR#822 (derived counters), /telemetry PR#831 (sampling controller)
- Confluence: Tracer Roadshow Notes (design artifacts and meeting slides)

Appendix: quick experiment logs (staging)
- 2028-11-28 10:00 JST: enabled dynamic sampling on staging (1.7k traces/min -> 1.1k traces/min).
- 2028-11-29 03:00 JST: noticed missing user-debug traces for kafka-fanout; added retention override rule.
- 2028-11-30 16:00 JST: dashboards switched to derived counters; alert noise reduced (5 noisy alerts -> 1 actionable).

End of doc.
